transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-28 14:30 UTC, Duration about 58 minutes. Attendees listed in metadata. Recording flagged as medium transcription quality.

Summary: quick status on access gates, review of last week's microbenchmarks (staging), alignment on KV cache warmup and SSO/KMS blockers, agreement to run a short canary and send detailed traces.

Topics: Access & VPC peering, SSO / KMS, benchmark anomalies (p95 spike), batching/quant profiles, next steps for canary rollforward.

00:00:05 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — aim to keep this tight, we've got an ask list.
00:00:12 Priya Nair: Thanks, Maya. Quick readout from our side, we've tried the initial VPC peer, hit a route blackhole between our staging nat and the redwood gateway, so staging can't reach the dedicated pool.
00:00:27 Daniel Park: Got it, Priya. On the Redwood side we saw a dropped route on the peering config — sometimes cloud console hides the propagated routes. We'll pull the traceroutes.
00:00:42 Liam O'Connor: yeah, traceroute attached in slack earlier but I can re-run with tcp syn to the gateway.
00:00:50 Zoe Tran: note — if your security policy blocks ephemeral egress to the gw nat, that will look like a blackhole. We had customers where the firewall was doing TLS inspection and dropping the KV cache warmup traffic.
00:01:10 Diego Ruiz: we don't do TLS inspection but we do have a strict outbound list. Is there a list of IPs/ports we need?
00:01:18 Jordan Li: we'll send the egress list. For staging the ports are 443 and a control plane websocket on 443 as well, but IPs are region-specific.
00:01:30 Maya Chen: moving to benchmarks — Daniel, you had the p95/p99 anomalies last Friday?
00:01:36 Daniel Park: yeah quick recap. We ran three jobs: single-request latencies, batched 4, and streaming. Single request median was 42ms, p95 jumped to 410ms in one run. p99 looked ok-ish 780ms — I know that sounds backwards, transcription again — point is there were outliers correlating with cold KV cache misses.
00:01:58 Priya Nair: hmm that's consistent with what we saw, some requests hit an empty KV cash — spelled like cash on the logs — so the model warmed slower. We warmed with a small prefix but maybe need longer warm-up.
00:02:12 Daniel Park: exactly. Our recommendation: increase warm-up prefix to ~512 tokens for initial seeding and enable the async KV prefetch that Redwood runtime exposes. That dropped p95 from 410 to 90 in our sim.
00:02:27 Sara Velasquez: async prefetch — any side effects on throughput or cost?
00:02:31 Daniel Park: small cost bump due to extra initial tokens, but net savings because fewer tail latency retries and less re-generation. For your e2e flows we estimate 4-7% token increase on warmup windows but 20-30% fewer tail retries.
00:02:45 Maya Chen: also model variant fallback talked about — when Dedicated capacity hits a spike we can route to a smaller quantized variant. Diego, any concerns with sending health data to second region?
00:02:58 Diego Ruiz: main concern is data residency and audit logs. If fallback crosses to a different region we need write-only audit logs back to our primary KMS and clear policy. Also need SOC2 artifact for cross-region fallback.
00:03:15 Maya Chen: understood. We can keep everything in region by using a spare Dedicated node in the same region; fallback will be within the same account. If for capacity reasons we absolutely need to go cross-region, we'll ensure KMS wrapping and double-logging.
00:03:32 Priya Nair: that helps. On SSO, our SAML assertion mapping didn't map groups correctly — users showed up as guest role which blocks dedicated api keys.
00:03:43 Jordan Li: we've seen SAML attribute mis-mapping before. If you send a sample assertion we can match the group attribute and provide a recommended mapping.
00:03:50 Priya Nair: I'll send an example.
00:03:54 Liam O'Connor: one more infra oddball: when we ran a local perf harness the client-side timers show ~20ms jitter before the request left the host. Could be our side, could be our host stack.
00:04:06 Daniel Park: that's important — client-side overhead sometimes inflates p95. Can you share the client metrics with timestamps so we can correlate with the server traces?
00:04:12 Liam O'Connor: yes will do.
00:04:18 Maya Chen: returning to bench numbers — we also saw a pattern where batches of 8 were worse than 4 for your mix. We think sequence length distribution causes dynamic kernel selection to recompile; that can cause spikes.
00:04:31 Daniel Park: action item — we'll attach the kernel-selection debug log. There's a small window where the runtime switches kernels and that causes a 100-200ms blip. If you have a narrow seq length distribution we can pin kernel choices or pre-warm the kernel cache.
00:04:45 Priya Nair: how do we pin kernel choices?
00:04:50 Daniel Park: config in the model manifest — set runtime.hint.kernel_prefer = "fast_small_seq" or set compile flags to force a single kernel. We'll include recommended manifest snippets in the follow-up.
00:05:02 Sara Velasquez: is that change non-disruptive?
00:05:05 Zoe Tran: it's non-disruptive, it's a config change on rollout; we recommend a canary first.
00:05:10 Maya Chen: speaking of canary — proposed window: run a 24 hour staging canary with 10% traffic to the quantized variant next week. If metrics look good we'll flip in staging then schedule a weekend cutover for production.
00:05:22 Priya Nair: timeline wise we want to avoid any service interruption in May. Is a weekend cutover acceptable?
00:05:27 Sara Velasquez: our product release is the following week so a weekend sounds fine.
00:05:32 Diego Ruiz: just require audit trail and rollback runbook.
00:05:36 Jordan Li: we'll provide the rollback script and an automated alert that re-routes to host fallback if SLO breached.
00:05:43 Daniel Park: quick note on KMS: we saw a policy mismatch — your KMS key didn't allow the Redwood service account to decrypt CSL wrapped logs. That manifests as 403s on key unwrap during model start.
00:05:55 Diego Ruiz: yes we saw the 403s but thought they were ephemeral.
00:05:58 Daniel Park: not ephemeral — need to add our service principal with kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions in the key policy.
00:06:06 Priya Nair: I'll give Diego the key id after the call, and he can add the policy.
00:06:10 Maya Chen: perfect. Next, a short discussion on cost tradeoffs — Dedicated baseline vs hosted. We sent a worksheet, any Qs?
00:06:21 Liam O'Connor: the delta looks large for 24/7 Dedicated. Do we have auto-burst options?
00:06:26 Maya Chen: yes, Dedicated supports burst pools and preemptible capacity to reduce cost. Also Optimize suggestions: quant-plus-caching typically reduces token spend ~30% for your workload.
00:06:38 Priya Nair: what's the quant quality drop? We care about hallucinations in clinical text.
00:06:43 Daniel Park: small but measurable. We ran the clinical prompt suite and saw no statistically significant degradation in entity extraction F1 at int8 quant on the 2B model, but for safety-critical tasks we'll keep int16 in canary. We'll tie quality alerts to the eval deck.
00:06:59 Sara Velasquez: can we attach the eval deck to the ticket?
00:07:02 Maya Chen: yes, will attach.
00:07:07 Priya Nair: any thoughts on data retention and logs? We need to keep inference logs for 90 days for internal audits.
00:07:14 Jordan Li: Redwood Console supports log retention tiers; for PII we can scrub and store salted hashes only. We'll provide retention policy options and a sample config.
00:07:24 Diego Ruiz: need assurance on who can access the raw traces — RBAC?
00:07:28 Zoe Tran: RBAC tied to SSO groups; audit logs show token-level access. We'll share a SOC2 artifact and an access matrix.
00:07:36 Priya Nair: great.
00:07:41 Maya Chen: wrapping to the next steps — agreed items: 1) Priya and Liam to re-run VPC/trace; 2) Daniel to produce the kernel and KV cache debug logs; 3) Redwood to share trimmed bench csv and p95/p99 traces; 4) plan the canary for 2026-05-05.
00:07:58 Liam O'Connor: one last small ask — can you include a 'what changed' delta from last week's config? It helps our change review board.
00:08:05 Maya Chen: yes we'll include a delta changelog.
00:08:10 Priya Nair: thanks — we'll aim to unblock KMS policy today.
00:08:14 Maya Chen: perfect. Any other blockers?
00:08:18 Diego Ruiz: none from security beyond KMS and audit questions.
00:08:22 Jordan Li: nothing else from ops.
00:08:25 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifact bundle. Meeting adjourned.
